newsitem.title: USA: Union pact ends San Francisco garbage strike.
newsitem.headline: Union pact ends San Francisco garbage strike.

text.p: Striking garbage collectors ratified a new labor contract Saturday, ending a strike that caused trash to pile up at homes across San Francisco, officials said.
Union members voted by a two-to-one margin to accept the new contract, which will boost workers' pay by 13.3 percent over five years and increase health care and pension benefits.
Average annual pay for a garbage collector is now $49,000.
"We addressed all of the concerns that we had," Robert Morales, secretary-treasurer of Teamsters Local 350, told reporters. "We're delighted that it was accepted."

The garbage collectors went on strike Thursday because of a dispute over pay and benefits. They had worked without a contract since Dec. 31. It was the city's first strike by garbage collectors in 57 years.

A tentative settlement was reached late Friday after two days of negotiations at City Hall between Norcal Waste Systems Inc. and union negotiators representing more than 500 striking garbage collectors.

Garbage company managers collected trash from hospitals, hotels, businesses and schools during the strike, but not from homes, where garbage started to pile up. City officials, fearing a prolonged strike could pose health risks, advised residents not to put garbage out on the curb.
Some striking workers could be back on the job by midday Saturday and normal service should be restored throughout the city by Monday, union and company officials said.
"Full service will quickly be restored," Norcal president Michael Sangiacomo said in a statement.
